long_biography.plain_text:
Christian Angermayer encountered RNA-interference research while studying at the University of Bayreuth and cofounded Ribopharma with two professors. He held a minority founder stake and sold it when Ribopharma merged with Alnylam in 2003, giving him his first substantial investment capital. He then moved from biotechnology entrepreneurship into company-building and capital allocation, founding Apeiron Investment Group in 2012.

Angermayer owns Apeiron, which invests its proprietary balance sheet in listed and private companies and also backs emerging asset managers through limited-partner commitments and minority general-partner stakes. Its focus ranges across biotechnology, fintech and cryptocurrency, deep technology, hospitality, sports, real estate and natural resources. Apeiron says it manages approximately $7 billion of internal and external capital. That figure includes money belonging to outside investors and is not Angermayer's personal net worth. Likewise, portfolio-company valuations, capital raised and corporate assets remain separate from his individual holdings. He continues to combine investing with founder and board roles in selected life-sciences companies.
